name: Cagrilintide
route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
status: Not FDA-approved. Phase 3 trials are under way; a semaglutide combination (CagriSema) is under FDA review
mechanism: Copies amylin, a pancreatic hormone released with insulin that signals fullness to the brain, in a form that lasts long enough for weekly dosing

article.summary: Cagrilintide is an investigational once-weekly amylin analog from Novo Nordisk that lowers appetite. It is being tested alone and with semaglutide as CagriSema, and is not FDA-approved.
article.takeaway: Cagrilintide is a long-acting copy of amylin, a hormone the pancreas releases with insulin that helps you feel full after a meal. In a 26-week phase 2 trial of 906 adults with overweight or obesity, the highest dose cut body weight by **10.8%** among people who took it as directed, compared with 3.0% on placebo and 9.0% on liraglutide 3.0 mg.[^1] Most of the large phase 3 data come from its combination with semaglutide, called [CagriSema](/peptides/cagrisema).[^2] Nausea is the most common side effect. Cagrilintide is not FDA-approved, and FDA says it cannot be used in compounding.[^3]
glance: Investigational; not approved by the FDA
Once-weekly injection under the skin (in trials)
Phase 2 trial; stand-alone phase 3 under way; phase 3 combination trials reported

blocks.text: Amylin is a hormone made by the same pancreatic cells that make insulin. After a meal it slows stomach emptying and acts on the brain to promote fullness. Natural amylin is short-lived, so cagrilintide is an engineered version built to last long enough for weekly injections. The older amylin drug [pramlintide](/peptides/pramlintide) is injected at mealtimes.
Amylin works through different brain circuits than GLP-1, the hormone copied by [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide). The idea behind CagriSema is that the two signals add to each other.

Novo Nordisk is developing cagrilintide on two tracks. On its own, a phase 3 weight-loss trial began in November 2025 and has finished enrolling.[^4] Combined with semaglutide in one weekly injection, as CagriSema, it was submitted to the FDA in December 2025, with a decision anticipated by late 2026.[^5] A phase 3 trial of cagrilintide and CagriSema in children and adolescents with excess weight began in January 2026.[^6]

rows: 906 adults with overweight or obesity, no diabetes
Weight change on cagrilintide 4.5 mg -10.8%; liraglutide 3.0 mg -9.0%; placebo -3.0% (taken as directed)[^1]
3,417 adults with obesity; one arm took cagrilintide alone
CagriSema -20.4% vs placebo -3.0%; the cagrilintide-alone arm was a comparison group[^2]
Reached BMI under 27 and waist-to-height ratio under 0.53: 9.0% on cagrilintide, 19.1% semaglutide, 30.3% CagriSema, 3.3% placebo[^7]

blocks.text: Across doses from 0.3 to 4.5 mg in the phase 2 trial, weight loss ranged from 6.0% to 10.8% and rose with dose.[^1]

items: **Digestive effects** were the main finding in phase 2: 41% to 63% of people on cagrilintide had a gastrointestinal event versus 32% on placebo, and nausea affected 20% to 47% versus 18%.[^1]
**Injection-site reactions** were also among the most frequent events.[^1]
**In REDEFINE 1,** digestive events occurred in 79.6% on CagriSema and 39.9% on placebo, mostly mild to moderate and temporary.[^2]

blocks.text: Long-term safety of cagrilintide alone is not yet established. The dedicated stand-alone phase 3 trial is still running, so most phase 3 information comes from one comparison arm of REDEFINE 1.

Cagrilintide is sold online by "research" vendors, but FDA states that it cannot be used in compounding under federal law because it is not a component of an approved drug. Products labeled for research use have been sold to consumers and are of unknown quality.[^3] Purity and dose cannot be verified.
Key events to watch are the FDA decision on CagriSema, results of the stand-alone cagrilintide phase 3 trial, and the first data in young people.[^5][^6]

evidence.label: Good for weight loss; mostly shown in combination
evidence.text: Cagrilintide alone has a randomized phase 2 trial and a phase 3 comparison arm,[^1][^2] but its dedicated stand-alone phase 3 trial is not finished. Most large-scale evidence concerns CagriSema, so cagrilintide's own long-term effects are less certain.

faq.q: How is cagrilintide different from semaglutide?
faq.a: Semaglutide copies the gut hormone GLP-1. Cagrilintide copies amylin, a different hormone that also signals fullness. Given together, they make CagriSema.[^2]
No. Neither cagrilintide alone nor CagriSema has FDA approval as of this writing. Novo Nordisk expected a decision on CagriSema by late 2026.[^5]
Not legally for human use. FDA says cagrilintide cannot be used in compounding, and research-labeled vials are unapproved and of unknown quality.[^3]
